description: Post-hoc reading of the 9 answers the grader marked wrong in run r1_c0 (GSM8K, zero-shot). Done after the run; it does not change the official, pre-registered score.
readers: 4 AI readers: Claude (the AI assistant that ran the experiment) and 3 more Claude sessions that did not see each other's verdicts. Their instructions and raw verdicts are in data/key_audit_readers.json. Not a human audit: read the questions yourself. Each item is also compared with GSM8K-Platinum (data/platinum_check.json), where people reviewed the questions its models got wrong.

key_change_notes.description: Post-hoc reading, by the assistant, of the answer keys GSM8K-Platinum changed among our 100 questions (compare GSM8K's and Platinum's worked solutions).

items.note: GSM8K's solution adds Julie's first-game score (10) instead of Sasha's (14). Sasha scored 14 + 4 = 18, the model's answer.
A truck that carries 2,000 pounds holds only 26 whole 75-pound flagstones, so 3 trucks carry 78 of the 80: 4 trucks are needed. The clear case.
Platinum counts Kayla herself as a guest (46 people instead of 45). A reasonable reading, but one you can argue with.

verdicts.model_error: the question is clear, the answer key is right, the model's answer is wrong
verdicts.key_error: the official answer key is wrong
verdicts.ambiguous_question: the question can reasonably be read two ways; the key and the model chose different readings
verdicts.grader_format: the model's number is right, but written in a form the exact-match grader rejects

items.reason: 'half of what is left is sold equally in the afternoon and evening': half of the 20 loaves split in two (5, the model) or all 20 split in two (10, the key).
'8 packs of 5 canvas bags for $4 each': $4 per pack (profit 288, the model) or $4 per bag (profit 160, the key).
The model set up the equations correctly, then counted one ingredient twice and answered 10/3 instead of 4.
Sasha scores 14 in game 1 and 10 - 6 = 4 in game 2, so 18 in total (the model's answer). The official solution adds Julie's 10 instead of Sasha's 14 and writes 14.
'How much does travel cost?' comes right after 'The tickets for travel cost...': the tickets (600, the model) or tickets plus supplies (1000, the key).
'depreciates at a constant rate of 21% per year': compounding (9,861, the model, the usual textbook reading) or 21% of the original price each year (7,400, the key).
'within an hour' may cover both puzzles (750, the key) or only the second one (500, the model). The weakest case: the key's reading is the more natural one.
The model treated the 20 toys still missing as the fifth worker's output (2 per hour) instead of 380 - 200 = 180 toys in 10 hours (18 per hour).
The model wrote '#### 8.00' and the key is 8. Exact match compares text, so both rules reject it.
